items.title: 71542_Bill Coleman autobiographical manuscript
items.q: I became acquainted with some of the musicians of Fess Williams' orchestra. Bobby Robinson played alto, Jelly James, trombone

ctx.x: We brought something new to the Savoy that was later copied by the Fess William's bunch and became a fad that every orchestra that played in the Savoy copied also. Cecil stood in front of the orchestra as did Fess Williams and he also wore a top hat and could do the Charleston while playing the tenor. But the rest of the musicians played sitting down. As the music stands were so high at the Savoy, Dickie Wells, Frank Newton and I decided that we would stand up when we had a solo. That made a hit with the public…

I became acquainted with some of the musicians of Fess Williams' orchestra. Bobby Robinson played alto, Jelly James, trombone; a little fellow called Stony played tenor. Kenneth Roane was the first trumpettist. The rest, I do not remember their names except George Temple whom I talked with and told him that I had seen him before. His brother was known as Red Temple. They were both light coloured and the brother had red hair.

After having played three days we were paid and the first thing I did was to go to 125th Street to a big shoe shop called Adler and buy myself a pair of shoes. Before that, I almost was ashamed to walk because I thought that people would see the hole in my shoe and I didn't dare to crook my leg for the same reason.
